producer_report.summary: Added docs/design/agent-and-build-slots.md. It reuses the existing code (parallel drain, `max_check_slots`, disk guard, `sccache` support, landing queue design) and splits agent slots from queued build slots. It measures a 5-job sample (35.0% model, 7.2% local build and test, 57.8% waiting) and states which jobs and directories were left out. It also finds that status.rs picks the newest landing record, which inflates the landing-and-rebuild stage (about 1337 min against 4.6 min to the first record in the sample). It sizes the machine at 1 build now and 2 after slot-owned warm target directories, with 12 to 16 agents, and lists 7 independently landable build jobs, each with files and a metric. `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` passes.

open_issues: Only 5 of the 14 landed-on-2026-11-04 jobs were read; the other 9 are listed by id as not read. A fuller sample would tighten the split.

Why later landing records re-list earlier jobs' commits, and whether the first record is the real merge, is inferred, not checked; build job 2 starts by confirming it against the pull request merge time.
All memory, CPU and filesystem figures are labeled estimates; no record or tool in this job measured them.
The body of the env.rs build-directory check (lexical or resolving links) was not read; the slot-directory symlink idea depends on it.
The plan-group size (cap on agents that can run side by side) is not measured.
Criterion 1 and the request say one file only, so CHANGELOG.md was left unchanged although the brief's changelog default and expected-deliverables list name it.
mistakes: I printed a whole landing record early (a 1300-line file) and spent budget; later queries used narrower patterns.
I first assumed the 14 landed jobs on 2026-11-04 would all be readable within budget; I read only 5 and the note says so.
learnings: status.rs `landing_record_time` takes the newest landing record that lists the job's commit, and one job's job_landing commit appears in many consecutive landing records (b4f5 is in 19 of 174). This makes the 'landing and rebuild' stage of ~1069 min mostly a result of record choice; the first record is 4 to 11 min after the verifier for the five sampled jobs.
`max_check_slots` exists in config.rs and disk.rs but is read only inside the disk formula; nothing in crates/athena-cli uses it, so no build count is enforced.
`athena.toml` has no [drain.pipeline] and sets [parallel] max_concurrency = 2; MAX_CONCURRENCY_CEILING is 8.
env.rs refuses a CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside the job directory (D46); policy.rs refuses cargo options that set build configuration.
In the 5 sampled jobs, 4 reused CI for all checks (0.0 s); the 'fails-without-N' checks in verification.json are the local build/test time (911m: 903 s).
No athena.build-measurement/1 records exist in the evidence snapshot's records/ directory, so the 10 to 12 GB per build is the request's figure, not a record.
The brief's expected deliverables list three filenames and CHANGELOG.md, but criterion 1 and the request say exactly one new file with no other path changed.
desires: A way to count directories (Glob and Grep show only 100 lines or per-file output), so exclusion counts could be exact instead of listed.
Read access to df, free, and the filesystem type on the real machine, to replace the memory, CPU and filesystem estimates.
Permission for Read and Grep on the tool-result overflow files, so large Grep outputs could be summed instead of re-queried.
